expectations.text: The image request is changed to ask the image service for a rendition sized to the on-screen cell (uses the ?w=/?h= resize params), not the raw 2000x3000 master URL
A cheap placeholder (solid color rect or one shared tiny texture) is shown while the image loads AND on load failure, never a blank gap or a second full image request per slot
expectations.evidence: shared opaque rect placeholder for loading AND failure

expectations.text: The answer explains that decode cost and texture memory are paid at the SOURCE image's pixel size regardless of the display size, so oversized images exhaust the GPU texture budget
expectations.evidence: explains decode+texture paid at source pixel size (~24MB/poster)

expectations.text: The answer references a concrete TV texture/RAM budget (e.g. tens of MB for all textures, ~1GB shared RAM, low-RAM device class) rather than treating memory as unbounded
expectations.evidence: cites 30-40MB texture budget, ~1GB shared RAM, low-RAM class

expectations.text: No suggestion relies on desktop-class headroom (e.g. 'just preload all images', 'increase the cache size') without the sizing fix
